name: Elicit
summary: Literature search and structured extraction over scientific papers, built for review work rather than summaries.
description:
Elicit does the tedious half of a systematic review: search across the scholarly corpus, screen by what the abstracts actually claim, then extract specified fields — population, intervention, outcomes, effect sizes — into a table you can audit. Column-by-column sourcing is the difference between a research assistant and a text generator, and it is where reviewers say the time is saved.

It is strongest in biomedical and social-science literature with good abstracts, and weaker where the useful numbers live only in a PDF's tables. Coverage of paywalled full text is limited by what the tool may legally read, so treat any extraction as a first pass with citations to verify, exactly as you would a human assistant's.
